known_limitations: The search is systematic and citation-chained but is not a registered systematic review.
Provisional saturation is based on fresh replacement Q11/Q12, not legacy Q1-Q10; it is search-coverage evidence rather than proof of absence.
Search interfaces do not expose stable raw database hit counts; fresh rounds therefore freeze unique primary candidates actually opened and screened.
Several arXiv works may later receive proceedings versions and require a final pre-submission refresh.
The SkillSmith primary PDF screenshot endpoint returned Cache miss; primary PDF text was inspected and locators are frozen, but a reviewer may re-open the PDF visually.
Exact per-experiment model tables for several older PDF papers remain a final-claim-freeze check; the structured table marks those fields without inventing values.
No producer-side validator or saturation result can establish priority wording or scientific novelty acceptance.
unexpected_findings: SIGIL is materially closer than the previous package recognized: it already combines typed IR, model/code ownership, source provenance, deterministic lowering, and a matched prose-versus-compiled execution comparison.
SkillRT, SkCC, Auto and related 2026 work show that typed/portable compiler-runtime skill territory is dense rather than represented by a single SkillSmith paper.
FACTS and Skill Discovery occupy offline deterministic/execution-verified reusable-artifact territory.
The Readout Shortcut provides direct prior evidence for the answer-copying alternative explanation in fixed 1-3B models.
The surviving flagship boundary is narrower: authoritative four-state semantic-result placement plus matched no-conclusion/copying controls and an independent layer oracle.
